In a 1977 interview with Country Music magazine — the same year she released one of her poppiest hits, “Here You Come Again” — Parton addressed the genre question head-on. “I never considered the fact that I was going pop,” she said at the time. “I will go pop, as far as crossing over, sooner or later. title: Galaxy Z Fold 8 is selling so well, Samsung is borrowing parts from the future
summary: The company is reportedly using future component reserves to fill the gap.
body: TL;DR Galaxy Z Fold 8 demand is reportedly outpacing Samsung’s expectations. A Display Driver IC (DDI) shortage is now putting pressure on Fold 8 production. Samsung is tapping future DDI reserves to keep making current Fold 8 units. Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra just became the best-selling Android phone globally in Q2 2026, while the regular Galaxy S26 also cracked the top 10. Now, Samsung has another phone that people apparently want more than it expected — so much so that the company is reportedly dipping into component stock reserved for future production to keep the Galaxy Z Fold 8 coming. According to ZDNet Korea , Samsung is running short of the Display Driver IC (DDI) used to control the pixels on the Galaxy Z Fold 8 OLED display. Samsung has reportedly increased its component orders after demand for the passport-style foldable exceeded expectations. But its DDI supplier, Taiwan’s United Microelectronics Corporation (UMC), has little room to ramp up production.

title: New Android 17 QPR2 feature lets you peek inside your phone’s secure sandbox
summary: Android 17 QPR2 Beta 4 introduces new Private Compute Core data logging controls inside Privacy Dashboard.
body: Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority TL;DR Android 17 QPR2 Beta 4 adds a dedicated “Data logging” menu for Private Compute Core within Privacy Dashboard. Users can toggle logging between Limited (up to three days/100MB) and Detailed (up to 12 hours/100MB) tiers, download logs, or delete them. Google rolled out Android 17 QPR2 Beta 4 , and alongside several under-the-hood tweaks, it introduces a major transparency upgrade for how the OS handles sensitive on-device data. The new release adds a dedicated “Data logging” section for the Private Compute Core right inside Privacy Dashboard. Private Compute Core is Android’s isolated sandbox that powers machine learning features such as Live Caption, Now Playing, and Smart Reply, without exposing user data directly to the cloud or other apps. While Private Compute Core has historically operated in a secure silo, this new Privacy Dashboard entry in Android 17 QPR2 Beta 4 lets users actively monitor, log, and review any outbound data leaving the Private Compute Core environment.

title: Google Messages has a bizarre bug that’s sending old texts to random people

body: TL;DR Some Google Messages users say old texts from unrelated conversations are unexpectedly resurfacing. Reports span multiple Pixel and Samsung phones. In some cases, those messages appear to be sent alongside new texts or images, raising serious privacy concerns. Google Messages is getting some welcome attention with custom chat themes and selective text copying finally becoming available, but the app’s recent run of bugs is taking some shine off those additions. Besides broken RCS messaging and conversations turning into multiple threads , users are reporting a more worrying problem: Messages appears to be pulling old texts from unrelated conversations and attaching or sending them with new messages. Several Reddit reports describe the same basic nightmare. In some cases, the stray text appears alongside a photo or group message. In others, users say the old message actually reaches the unintended recipient.

body: Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority TL;DR Android 17 QPR2 Beta 4, which was released last week, brings an easier way to broadcast your voice over a private network. The new Audio broadcast feature expands Pixels’ existing Auracast-based media-sharing features to transmit audio over Bluetooth LE Audio. While the feature was introduced last month, it is now much easier to access. Google is in the final legs of testing Android 17 QPR2 Beta before a significant feature drop for Pixels in September. Last Friday, it released the fourth QPR2 Beta, sorting out a long list of bugs and usability issues from previous beta builds. As part of Android 17 QPR2 Beta 4 , Google is adding a few useful features that didn’t make it into the changelog, including easier access to Voice Broadcast. Voice Broadcast on Pixel devices with Android 17 QPR2 Beta is like a personal PA system. It lets users voice their views over, or share audio from a media player, in private listening channels. This private network is enabled by Bluetooth LE (Low Energy), and audio devices — earbuds and such — used by recipients must support the technology.

title: Lake Ontario is now ‘Lake America’ on Google Maps, but not for everyone
summary: US citizen will see the "new" name, while Canadians still see "Lake Ontario."
body: Credit: Andy Walker / Android Authority TL;DR Google Maps is now starting to call Lake Ontario “Lake America” following recent executive orders. Last week, President Trump signed the executive order to rename the lake officially. Google says the new change is only visible for people in the US, while those in Canada will continue to see “Lake Ontario.” Last week, US President Donald Trump signed executive orders to officially rename Lake Ontario “Lake America,” his second re-christening, so to speak, of a body of water after the Gulf of Mexico . Following these official orders, Google Maps has started showing the name of the body of water bordering both the US and Canada. In an official announcement , Google noted it will start showing the lake’s new official name, as designated by the US Geographic Names Information System (GNIS). body: If there are two pieces of tech I have a love-hate relationship with, it’s USB-C charging and Google’s Pixel smartphones. Based on my previous experiences with Pixels, testing the 45W wired charging capabilities of the new Pixel 11 Pro XL was almost certainly going to cause a headache or two, but it quickly descended into a full-on migraine. Let’s start with the good USB-C news for the Pixel 11 Pro XL. After years of underperforming the headline charging figure, Google’s latest large flagship comes much closer to hitting its 45W marketing claim. While still not quite there, I was able to hit a peak of 40.7W for about the first 9 minutes on the Google Pixel Flex 67W charger (). That’s a reasonable power level and far better sustained than rivals that claim up to 100W capabilities, plus it exceeds the 35W peak I’ve observed on the previous two generations of XL smartphones. title: Meta fixes distressingly obvious smart glasses recording LED loophole
summary: You won't believe how easy it was to bypass Meta privacy protections.
body: TL;DR Meta’s smart glasses attempt to detect when their recording LED is blocked or tampered with, and will refuse to start filming. It turns out this check was only performed when recordings were initiated, and users could just start filming and cover the LED afterwards. Meta is currently rolling out a fix to correct this behavior. Retro gamers may remember the old PlayStation 1 swap trick: The system would only check disc integrity when first booting, so you could run imports or backups by first powering the PlayStation up with a legit disc in it, and then quickly swapping it out. It turns out that Meta’s smart glasses have been vulnerable to a similar attack, and the company is only just now getting around to patching it.
